# ============================================================
# REGEX IN R CHEAT SHEET
# ============================================================
# Regex = regular expressions
# Regex is used to find patterns in text.
#
# In R, regex is commonly used with stringr functions:
#
# str_detect()      # TRUE/FALSE: does this pattern exist?
# str_extract()     # pulls out the first match
# str_extract_all() # pulls out all matches
# str_replace()     # replaces first match
# str_replace_all() # replaces all matches
# str_count()       # counts matches
# str_split()       # splits text using a pattern
#
# Load stringr:
library(stringr)
# ============================================================
# 1. BASIC STRINGR FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================

text <- "Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem in 1 AD."

# Detect whether pattern exists
str_detect(text, "Jesus")
# TRUE

# Extract first match
str_extract(text, "Jesus")
# "Jesus"

# Extract all matches
str_extract_all(text, "in")
# "in" "in"

# Replace first match
str_replace(text, "Jesus", "The Savior")

# Replace all matches
str_replace_all(text, "in", "INSIDE")

# Count matches
str_count(text, "in")

# Split text
str_split(text, " ")
# ============================================================
# 2. IMPORTANT REGEX SYMBOLS
# ============================================================

# .        any single character
# \\d      any digit, 0-9
# \\D      anything that is NOT a digit
# \\w      word character: letters, numbers, underscore
# \\W      anything that is NOT a word character
# \\s      whitespace: space, tab, newline
# \\S      anything that is NOT whitespace
#
# ^        start of string
# $        end of string
#
# *        0 or more
# +        1 or more
# ?        0 or 1
#
# {n}      exactly n times
# {n,}     n or more times
# {n,m}    between n and m times
#
# []       character set
# [^]      not these characters
# |        OR
# ()       group
# ============================================================
# 3. WHY R USES DOUBLE BACKSLASHES
# ============================================================

# In normal regex, digit is:
# \d
#
# But in R strings, you need:
# "\\d"
#
# Because R uses backslash for escape characters.
# So regex patterns often need double backslashes.

text <- "I have 3 dogs and 12 fish."

str_extract_all(text, "\\d+")
# Extracts: "3" "12"
# ============================================================
# 4. DIGITS AND NUMBERS
# ============================================================

text <- "The prices are $5, $12, and $100."

# Find one digit
str_extract_all(text, "\\d")
# "5" "1" "2" "1" "0" "0"

# Find full numbers
str_extract_all(text, "\\d+")
# "5" "12" "100"

# Find exactly 2 digits
str_extract_all(text, "\\d{2}")
# "12" "10"

# Find 1 or more digits
str_extract_all(text, "\\d+")

# Find numbers with decimals
text2 <- "The values are 4.5, 10.25, and 7."

str_extract_all(text2, "\\d+\\.\\d+")
# "4.5" "10.25"

# Find numbers with optional decimals
str_extract_all(text2, "\\d+(\\.\\d+)?")
# "4.5" "10.25" "7"
# ============================================================
# 5. LETTERS AND WORDS
# ============================================================

text <- "Nephi saw 3 visions."

# Find word characters
str_extract_all(text, "\\w+")
# "Nephi" "saw" "3" "visions"

# Find letters only
str_extract_all(text, "[A-Za-z]+")
# "Nephi" "saw" "visions"

# Find uppercase letters
str_extract_all(text, "[A-Z]")
# "N"

# Find lowercase letters
str_extract_all(text, "[a-z]+")
# "ephi" "saw" "visions"

# Find words that start with capital letter
text2 <- "Nephi and Lehi went to Jerusalem."

str_extract_all(text2, "[A-Z][a-z]+")
# "Nephi" "Lehi" "Jerusalem"
# ============================================================
# 6. WHITESPACE
# ============================================================

text <- "Hello     world"

# Find spaces
str_extract_all(text, "\\s+")

# Replace multiple spaces with one space
str_replace_all(text, "\\s+", " ")
# "Hello world"

# Remove all whitespace
str_replace_all(text, "\\s+", "")
# "Helloworld"
# ============================================================
# 7. START AND END OF STRING
# ============================================================

text <- c("apple pie", "banana bread", "apple juice", "grape apple")

# Starts with apple
str_detect(text, "^apple")
# TRUE FALSE TRUE FALSE

# Ends with apple
str_detect(text, "apple$")
# FALSE FALSE FALSE TRUE

# Starts with apple OR banana
str_detect(text, "^(apple|banana)")
# TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE

# Ends with pie OR bread
str_detect(text, "(pie|bread)$")
# TRUE TRUE FALSE FALSE
# ============================================================
# 8. CHARACTER SETS []
# ============================================================

text <- "cat, bat, rat, mat, dog"

# Match cat, bat, or rat
str_extract_all(text, "[cbr]at")
# "cat" "bat" "rat"

# Match anything ending in at
str_extract_all(text, ".at")
# "cat" "bat" "rat" "mat"

# Match vowels
str_extract_all(text, "[aeiou]")
# "a" "a" "a" "a" "o"

# Match anything that is NOT a vowel
str_extract_all(text, "[^aeiou]")
# ============================================================
# 9. OR WITH |
# ============================================================

text <- "I like cats and dogs."

# Detect cat OR dog
str_detect(text, "cat|dog")
# TRUE

# Extract cat OR dog
str_extract_all(text, "cat|dog")
# "cat" "dog"

# Extract cats OR dogs
str_extract_all(text, "cats|dogs")
# "cats" "dogs"
# ============================================================
# 10. GROUPS WITH ()
# ============================================================

text <- "Jesus Christ, Lord Jesus, Savior Jesus"

# Match either Jesus Christ or Lord Jesus
str_extract_all(text, "(Jesus Christ|Lord Jesus)")
# "Jesus Christ" "Lord Jesus"

# Groups are useful when using OR with longer phrases
# ============================================================
# 11. WORD BOUNDARIES
# ============================================================

# \\b means word boundary.
# It helps match whole words only.

text <- c("he", "the", "hello", "he is here")

# Detect "he" anywhere
str_detect(text, "he")
# TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE

# Detect "he" as a whole word
str_detect(text, "\\bhe\\b")
# TRUE FALSE FALSE TRUE

# This matters a lot.
# Without word boundaries, "he" matches inside "the" and "hello".
# ============================================================
# 12. CASE SENSITIVITY
# ============================================================

text <- c("Jesus", "jesus", "JESUS")

# Normal regex is case-sensitive
str_detect(text, "Jesus")
# TRUE FALSE FALSE

# Ignore case
str_detect(text, regex("jesus", ignore_case = TRUE))
# TRUE TRUE TRUE
# ============================================================
# 13. ESCAPING SPECIAL CHARACTERS
# ============================================================

# Some characters have special regex meanings:
#
# . ^ $ * + ? ( ) [ ] { } | \
#
# If you want the literal character, escape it with \\

text <- "The file is report.pdf"

# WRONG: "." means any character
str_detect(text, ".pdf")

# RIGHT: "\\." means a literal period
str_detect(text, "\\.pdf")

# Find dollar signs
text2 <- "The price is $25."

str_detect(text2, "\\$")
# TRUE

# Find parentheses
text3 <- "Call me at (555) 123-4567."

str_extract(text3, "\\(555\\)")
# "(555)"
# ============================================================
# 14. COMMON PATTERNS
# ============================================================

# Any number:
"\\d+"

# Decimal number:
"\\d+\\.\\d+"

# Optional decimal:
"\\d+(\\.\\d+)?"

# Any word:
"\\w+"

# Letters only:
"[A-Za-z]+"

# Capitalized word:
"[A-Z][a-z]+"

# Whitespace:
"\\s+"

# Whole word "the":
"\\bthe\\b"

# Starts with "A":
"^A"

# Ends with ".":
"\\.$"

# Email-ish pattern:
"\\w+@\\w+\\.\\w+"

# Phone number like 555-123-4567:
"\\d{3}-\\d{3}-\\d{4}"

# Date like 2026-07-03:
"\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}"
# ============================================================
# 15. EXTRACTING DATES
# ============================================================

text <- "The dates are 2026-07-03 and 2027-12-15."

str_extract_all(text, "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")
# "2026-07-03" "2027-12-15"

# Pattern explanation:
# \\d{4}  = four digits
# -       = literal dash
# \\d{2}  = two digits
# -       = literal dash
# \\d{2}  = two digits
# ============================================================
# 16. EXTRACTING PHONE NUMBERS
# ============================================================

text <- "Call 555-123-4567 or 801-555-9999."

str_extract_all(text, "\\d{3}-\\d{3}-\\d{4}")
# "555-123-4567" "801-555-9999"

# Pattern explanation:
# \\d{3} = exactly 3 digits
# -      = dash
# \\d{3} = exactly 3 digits
# -      = dash
# \\d{4} = exactly 4 digits
# ============================================================
# 17. EXTRACTING EMAILS
# ============================================================

text <- "Email me at student@byui.edu or help@example.com."

str_extract_all(text, "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")
# "student@byui.edu" "help@example.com"

# Simpler but less accurate:
str_extract_all(text, "\\w+@\\w+\\.\\w+")
# ============================================================
# 18. REPLACING TEXT
# ============================================================

text <- "My phone number is 555-123-4567."

# Replace phone number with hidden version
str_replace_all(text, "\\d{3}-\\d{3}-\\d{4}", "XXX-XXX-XXXX")
# "My phone number is XXX-XXX-XXXX."

# Replace all digits with X
str_replace_all(text, "\\d", "X")
# "My phone number is XXX-XXX-XXXX."
# ============================================================
# 19. SPLITTING TEXT
# ============================================================

text <- "apple,banana,orange"

str_split(text, ",")
# splits into apple banana orange

text2 <- "apple banana    orange"

str_split(text2, "\\s+")
# splits on one or more spaces
# ============================================================
# 20. COUNTING WORDS
# ============================================================

text <- "The Savior loves the people."

# Count spaces + 1
str_count(text, " ") + 1
# 5

# Better: count words
str_count(text, "\\w+")
# 5

# Count a specific word
str_count(text, "\\bthe\\b")
# 1 because lowercase "the" only

# Ignore case
str_count(str_to_lower(text), "\\bthe\\b")
# 2
# ============================================================
# 21. COUNTING PHRASES
# ============================================================

text <- "Jesus Christ is the Son of God. I believe in Jesus Christ."

str_count(text, "Jesus Christ")
# 2

# Ignore case
str_count(str_to_lower(text), "jesus christ")
# 2
# ============================================================
# 22. MATCHING MULTIPLE PHRASES
# ============================================================

text <- "Jesus Christ is Lord and Savior."

pattern <- "Jesus Christ|Lord|Savior"

str_extract_all(text, pattern)
# "Jesus Christ" "Lord" "Savior"

str_count(text, pattern)
# 3
# ============================================================
# 23. USING A VECTOR OF WORDS OR PHRASES
# ============================================================

names <- c("Jesus Christ", "Lord", "Savior", "Redeemer")

text <- "Jesus Christ is my Savior and Redeemer."

# Collapse names into one regex pattern separated by OR
pattern <- paste(names, collapse = "|")

pattern
# "Jesus Christ|Lord|Savior|Redeemer"

str_extract_all(text, pattern)
# "Jesus Christ" "Savior" "Redeemer"
# ============================================================
# 24. IMPORTANT: ESCAPE SPECIAL CHARACTERS IN A VECTOR
# ============================================================

# If your search terms contain punctuation, escape them.

terms <- c("God's Son", "Lord.", "Savior?")

escaped_terms <- str_replace_all(terms, "([\\W])", "\\\\\\1")

escaped_terms

pattern <- paste(escaped_terms, collapse = "|")

text <- "I believe in God's Son. He is Lord. Is He Savior?"

str_extract_all(text, pattern)
# ============================================================
# 25. UNDERSTANDING THIS ESCAPE CODE
# ============================================================

str_replace_all(terms, "([\\W])", "\\\\\\1")

# This is advanced, but here is the idea:
#
# [\\W] means:
#   find any non-word character
#   punctuation, spaces, apostrophes, periods, question marks, etc.
#
# () means:
#   capture what you found
#
# "\\\\\\1" means:
#   put a backslash before the thing you found
#
# So:
# "Lord."
# becomes:
# "Lord\\."
#
# That way the period is treated as a real period,
# not the regex symbol for "any character".
# ============================================================
# 26. GREEDY VS LAZY MATCHING
# ============================================================

text <- "Start here. Stop here. Really stop here."

# Greedy: grabs as much as possible
str_extract(text, "Start.*Stop")
# May grab too much

# Lazy: grabs as little as possible
str_extract(text, "Start.*?Stop")

# .* means:
#   any character, 0 or more times
#
# .*? means:
#   any character, 0 or more times, but as little as possible
# ============================================================
# 27. EXTRACT EVERYTHING BEFORE OR AFTER SOMETHING
# ============================================================

text <- "Name: Nephi"

# Extract everything before colon
str_extract(text, ".*(?=:)")
# "Name"

# Extract everything after colon and space
str_extract(text, "(?<=: ).*")
# "Nephi"

# (?=...) is lookahead
# (?<=...) is lookbehind
#
# These are advanced. Use only if needed.
# ============================================================
# 28. COMMON STRING CLEANING TASKS
# ============================================================

text <- "   Hello     world!!!   "

# Remove extra spaces at beginning/end
str_trim(text)

# Replace multiple spaces with one space
str_squish(text)

# Make lowercase
str_to_lower(text)

# Make uppercase
str_to_upper(text)

# Remove punctuation
str_replace_all(text, "[[:punct:]]", "")

# Remove digits
str_replace_all(text, "\\d", "")

# Remove letters
str_replace_all(text, "[A-Za-z]", "")
# ============================================================
# 29. CHARACTER CLASSES IN R
# ============================================================

# [[:digit:]]  digits
# [[:alpha:]]  letters
# [[:alnum:]]  letters and digits
# [[:space:]]  spaces
# [[:punct:]]  punctuation
# [[:lower:]]  lowercase letters
# [[:upper:]]  uppercase letters

text <- "Hello!!! 123"

str_extract_all(text, "[[:digit:]]+")
# "123"

str_extract_all(text, "[[:alpha:]]+")
# "Hello"

str_replace_all(text, "[[:punct:]]", "")
# "Hello 123"
# ============================================================
# 30. REGEX WITH FILTER()
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)

df <- tibble(
  name = c("Apple", "Banana", "Apricot", "Grape"),
  price = c(1, 2, 3, 4)
)

# Keep rows where name starts with A
df %>%
  filter(str_detect(name, "^A"))

# Keep rows where name contains "ap", ignoring case
df %>%
  filter(str_detect(name, regex("ap", ignore_case = TRUE)))

# Remove rows where name contains "Banana"
df %>%
  filter(!str_detect(name, "Banana"))
# ============================================================
# 31. REGEX WITH MUTATE()
# ============================================================

df <- tibble(
  code = c("CA-2020", "ID-2021", "UT-2022")
)

df %>%
  mutate(
    state = str_extract(code, "^[A-Z]{2}"),
    year = str_extract(code, "\\d{4}")
  )

# Explanation:
# ^[A-Z]{2} = two capital letters at the start
# \\d{4}    = four digits
# ============================================================
# 32. REGEX WITH SEPARATE-LIKE WORK
# ============================================================

df <- tibble(
  quarter = c("2017 Q1", "2017 Q2", "2018 Q1")
)

df %>%
  mutate(
    year = str_extract(quarter, "\\d{4}"),
    qtr = str_extract(quarter, "Q\\d")
  )

# year gets 2017, 2018, etc.
# qtr gets Q1, Q2, etc.
# ============================================================
# 33. QUICK GUIDE: WHICH FUNCTION DO I USE?
# ============================================================

# I need TRUE/FALSE:
str_detect()

# I need to pull out text:
str_extract()

# I need all matches:
str_extract_all()

# I need to replace text:
str_replace()
str_replace_all()

# I need to count matches:
str_count()

# I need to split text:
str_split()

# I need to remove spaces:
str_trim()
str_squish()

# I need to change case:
str_to_lower()
str_to_upper()
# ============================================================
# 34. QUICK GUIDE: WHICH PATTERN DO I USE?
# ============================================================

# Any digit:
"\\d"

# Full number:
"\\d+"

# Any letter:
"[A-Za-z]"

# Any word:
"\\w+"

# Any spaces:
"\\s+"

# Whole word:
"\\bword\\b"

# Starts with:
"^pattern"

# Ends with:
"pattern$"

# OR:
"cat|dog"

# One or more:
"+"

# Zero or more:
"*"

# Optional:
"?"

# Exact count:
"{3}"

# Between counts:
"{2,4}"
# ============================================================
# 35. COMMON ERRORS
# ============================================================

# ERROR 1:
# Using "\d" instead of "\\d"

str_extract_all("abc123", "\d")
# This may error or not work correctly.

# Correct:
str_extract_all("abc123", "\\d")


# ERROR 2:
# Forgetting that "." means any character

text <- "file.pdf"

str_detect(text, ".pdf")
# This can match more than you mean.

# Correct:
str_detect(text, "\\.pdf")


# ERROR 3:
# Forgetting word boundaries

text <- c("he", "the", "hello")

str_detect(text, "he")
# TRUE TRUE TRUE

# Correct if you only want the word "he":
str_detect(text, "\\bhe\\b")
# TRUE FALSE FALSE


# ERROR 4:
# Putting fixed colors inside aes()

# Wrong:
ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = price, fill = "blue")) +
  geom_col()

# Better:
ggplot(df, aes(x = name, y = price)) +
  geom_col(fill = "blue")
# ============================================================
# 36. MINI PRACTICE EXAMPLES
# ============================================================

text <- "Order #123 was placed on 2026-07-03 by john@email.com."

# Extract order number
str_extract(text, "#\\d+")
# "#123"

# Extract order number without #
str_extract(text, "\\d+")

# Extract date
str_extract(text, "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}")

# Extract email
str_extract(text, "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")

# Replace email
str_replace(text, "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[hidden email]")
# ============================================================
# 37. REGEX MENTAL CHECKLIST
# ============================================================

# 1. What am I trying to find?
#    digits, words, dates, punctuation, spaces, phrases?
#
# 2. Do I need one match or all matches?
#    one match = str_extract()
#    all matches = str_extract_all()
#
# 3. Do I need TRUE/FALSE?
#    str_detect()
#
# 4. Do I need to replace something?
#    str_replace_all()
#
# 5. Does my pattern use backslashes?
#    In R, use double backslash.
#    "\\d", "\\s", "\\b", "\\."
#
# 6. Do I need whole words only?
#    Use "\\bword\\b"
#
# 7. Do I need to ignore case?
#    regex("pattern", ignore_case = TRUE)
# ============================================================
# 38. MOST USEFUL REGEX EXAMPLES FOR CLASS
# ============================================================

# Extract year from "2017 Q1"
str_extract("2017 Q1", "\\d{4}")
# "2017"

# Extract quarter from "2017 Q1"
str_extract("2017 Q1", "Q\\d")
# "Q1"

# Extract state from "CA-2010"
str_extract("CA-2010", "^[A-Z]{2}")
# "CA"

# Extract number from "Sales: 483"
str_extract("Sales: 483", "\\d+")
# "483"

# Remove commas from numbers
str_replace_all("1,250,000", ",", "")
# "1250000"

# Remove dollar signs
str_replace_all("$25.99", "\\$", "")
# "25.99"

# Remove percent signs
str_replace_all("45%", "%", "")
# "45"

# Keep only digits
str_extract_all("abc123def456", "\\d+")[[1]]
# "123" "456"
# ============================================================
# 39. REMEMBER THIS
# ============================================================

# Regex pattern:
"\\d+"

# stringr function:
str_extract(text, "\\d+")

# tidyverse use:
data %>%
  mutate(number = str_extract(text_column, "\\d+"))

# filter use:
data %>%
  filter(str_detect(text_column, "pattern"))

# replace use:
data %>%
  mutate(clean_text = str_replace_all(text_column, "pattern", "replacement"))
# ============================================================
# 40. THE BIGGEST REGEX MEMORY TRICK
# ============================================================

# In R:
#
# "\\d+" means:
#   one or more digits
#
# "\\s+" means:
#   one or more spaces
#
# "\\w+" means:
#   one or more word characters
#
# "\\bword\\b" means:
#   the whole word "word"
#
# "\\." means:
#   a real period
#
# "^word" means:
#   starts with word
#
# "word$" means:
#   ends with word
#
# "cat|dog" means:
#   cat OR dog
#
# "[A-Z]" means:
#   one capital letter
#
# "[A-Za-z]+" means:
#   one or more letters
#
# "\\d{4}" means:
#   exactly four digits

For your class, the highest-value things to memorize are:

str_detect()
str_extract()
str_replace_all()
str_count()
pivot_longer()
mutate(year = str_extract(column, "\\d{4}"))
"\\d+"
"\\d{4}"
"\\s+"
"\\bword\\b"
"[A-Za-z]+"
